minutes.headline: Committee previews an FY27 school budget gap likely needing an override; also OK'd a costly France trip.
minutes.summary: The committee heard the superintendent's report (snow-day decisions, YTD spending, new Director of Teaching and Learning), then spent most of the meeting on money: a debated and approved France/Switzerland trip, a federal entitlement grants review flagging risk to Title I/II/IV and special-education grant funding, and a wide-ranging discussion of the FY27 budget, a likely override, and Turkey Hill's building future via the MSBA. Two routine policies (middle school pathway exploration; competency determination) passed on third read, and Turkey Hill accessibility needs were flagged as needing near-term attention regardless of the MSBA timeline.

votes.motion: Accept the Hannaford Helps donations for the middle school and the primary school
Approve and make official the Middle School Pathway Exploration policy (5201.03) and the Lunenburg Competency Determination policy (5204.01)

budget_items.what_was_said: A warrant covering roughly November 17 to December 1 was presented for routine approval; no line-item transfers accompanied it so no vote was required.
A donation was made to the Lunenburg Primary School via the Hannaford Helps program for field trips and presentations.
A companion donation was made for middle school student programming.
The superintendent reported year-to-date expenditures and flagged a possible reclassification at the next meeting that would raise the percentage spent, still leaving a healthy position.
The trip is planned for April 2027, with monthly payments to spread the cost for families.

budget_items.topic: France/Switzerland trip - comparison to prior trips
budget_items.what_was_said: The presenting teacher said the cost was comparable to previous world-language trips.
A member noted the existing per-sport athletic fee as a comparison point for the trip's affordability debate.
Members recalled a prior Galapagos trip's cost while discussing rising travel-trip prices.
The teacher said she negotiated with the tour company, including removal of a surcharge, to keep the trip under a stated ceiling.

budget_items.topic: Title I grant - FY25 surge and reversion
budget_items.what_was_said: Title I funding spiked in FY25 relative to baseline, then fell below the FY24 baseline the following year; the district called FY25 an outlier.

budget_items.topic: Title I grant - FY27 planning baseline
budget_items.what_was_said: The district recommended budgeting Title I conservatively rather than averaging the volatile three-year trend.

budget_items.topic: Title I grant - FY26 vs FY24
budget_items.what_was_said: FY26 Title I funding came in only slightly below FY24 in dollar terms, though inflation eroded its real value further.

budget_items.topic: Title I grant - share of budget
budget_items.what_was_said: A member noted the Title I amounts represent a small share of the overall budget.
Title II funding for professional development dropped year over year, directly reducing available training and conference spending.

budget_items.topic: Title II grant - FY27 planning baseline
budget_items.what_was_said: The district proposed shifting to a train-the-trainer PD model given constrained Title II funds.
Title IV is a small, relatively stable grant usable for student support, enrichment and technology, described as foldable into Title I.

budget_items.topic: Title IV grant - FY27 planning baseline
budget_items.what_was_said: The district will budget Title IV using a conservative baseline for targeted, low-recurring purchases.

budget_items.topic: Federal entitlement grants - cumulative purchasing-power loss
budget_items.what_was_said: The district estimated a loss of real purchasing power across its federal entitlement grants once inflation, steps and cost-of-living adjustments are accounted for.
These special-education federal grants have stayed steady over three years and currently fund out-of-district tuition; the district said it cannot afford to lose the staffing capacity they represent.
figures_as_heard: two and a half to three and a half full-time equivalent

budget_items.what_was_said: Facilities-related capital cost figures for Turkey Hill work (windows, mini-splits, doors, accessibility) were discussed, with more than one figure mentioned for the scope of work.
A member recounted that installing central AC originally would have cost far less than the later mini-split retrofit, illustrating the cost of deferring building investment.
The PTO is selling a limited run of branded blankets as a fundraiser ahead of Christmas.

decisions.decision: Approval of the October 15, 2025 regular session minutes was pushed to the next meeting.
An update on kindergarten/1st/2nd grade reading levels will be given at a future meeting once updated internal assessment data is available (expected January).
Principals will provide updates on their school improvement plans.
The winter athletics report was pulled from tonight's docket and will be presented at the next meeting.
The school calendar presented tonight is a first draft; it will go to principals/school councils and be posted publicly for feedback before a vote.

A full discussion of combining the athletic director and athletic trainer roles, including input from Ms. Burns (Shannina), will occur at the December 17 budget workshop before budget decisions are finalized.
The district will pursue a Massachusetts School Building Authority statement of intent for Turkey Hill targeting an April 2027 (not April 2026) submission.
The chair said the committee will wait for the MSBA process rather than pursue a competitive application this year.
The town's unused debt capacity (as distinct from a debt exclusion) and capital strategy will be discussed at the next tri-board meeting.
Mandy was designated to reach out to other (non-regional, similarly sized) school committees to explore a shared advocacy coalition on state funding.
The next tri-board meeting date has not yet been set; staff will follow up to schedule it.
Staff will try to compile a list of lower-cost Turkey Hill accessibility upgrades, likely by January, to scope near-term spending options.

what_happened.line: Committee said the FY27 school budget likely needs an override, with further work at a December 17 budget workshop.
Committee approved a France/Switzerland trip after debate over cost and equity, though the vote outcome was not clearly audible on the recording.
A federal grants review flagged risk to Title I, Title II, Title IV and special-education funding, recommending conservative FY27 budgeting for those grants.
District will pursue a Massachusetts School Building Authority statement of intent for Turkey Hill targeting an April 2027 submission rather than a competitive application this year.
Two policies -- middle school pathway exploration and competency determination -- passed on third read.

why_it_matters: An override would ask residents to vote on raising taxes above the levy cap to close the FY27 school budget gap.
Federal grant risk to Title I/II/IV and special education could shift costs onto the town-funded school budget if those funds shrink.
The Turkey Hill building decision sets the timeline and state-funding path for any future renovation or construction, which affects future borrowing and tax bills.
watch_next: April 2027 MSBA statement-of-intent submission for Turkey Hill
